Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking our call last week. Our procurement team has pulled together a short list of security and data residency requirements we'd need Redwood to confirm before we can move to contract. Primary asks:

- Confirmation that all inference and persistent storage for RegulaHealth customer payloads will remain in EU regions only (data residency).
- Evidence / artifacts for SCCs implementation and any supplementary technical controls intended to mitigate cross-border access risk (per Schrems II).
- Retention and deletion SLA: we need confirmation of deletion timelines and an explanation of backups/replication behavior (including logs and snapshots).
- Whether RegulaHealth can use customer-managed keys (KMS) for data at rest and key exclusivity options.

Please find attached our procurement_requirements.pdf — it includes the timeline (we need vendor answers by 2027-07-05) and the legal points procurement will require in the SOW.

Could you provide a short gap analysis and a proposed timeline for any controls you cannot immediately attest to? Also let us know if you prefer a technical handoff call with your compliance team.

Best,
Marta Jensen
Head of Procurement, RegulaHealth

Hi Marta,

Thanks — and really appreciate the timeline. I've pulled together initial answers and attached a short processing summary and a preliminary gap analysis spreadsheet that maps your asks to our current controls. Quick highlights:

- EU-only processing: Redwood supports region pinning; for RegulaHealth we can pin inference, embeddings, and persistent customer storage to our EU geography (Frankfurt, Paris). That covers live inference and model caches.

- Backups & snapshots: automated backups for persistent stores are retained in-region, however our current cross-region disaster recovery snapshot copy is optional and disabled by default for private deployments. For Hosted customers we offer optional cross-region DR; we can disable for your tenant and document as a contract commitment.

- SCCs / Schrems II: we use the standard EU SCCs and maintain a controls catalogue. Technical mitigations we reference include: strict routing by tenant, in-region KV cache, and access governance for support engineers. That said, there are two items flagged in the preliminary gap analysis where we need legal sign-off or slight engineering changes: 1) certified customer-managed KMS for hosted tenants (we currently support CMEK for Dedicated and Private; Hosted support is in roadmap); 2) formal attestation language around human access to logs containing customer identifiers.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 45-minute call with our privacy lead (Aditya Rao) and an engineering tech lead to walk through the gap analysis — can we do 2027-07-02 10:00 CEST?
2) We will prepare a short contract appendix that commits to EU-only routing and disables cross-region snapshot copy for RegulaHealth.
3) Aditya and Laura will draft recommended language for the SCCs addendum and an engineering timeline for CMEK support in Hosted if you require it.

I've attached: redwood-processing-summary.pdf and redwood_prelim_gap_analysis.xlsx.

If that schedule looks tight, we can push to the week of 2027-07-05 but we want to keep within your procurement window.

Thanks — and looping the team in now.

— Stephanie Nguyen

Hi Marta / team,

Appreciate the clear asks. A few clarifications and proposed commitments from our side:

1) SCCs and legal posture
- We operate under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (controller-to-processor and processor-to-subprocessor flows where applicable). For procurement, we can provide a signed SCCs annex and our controls mapping doc.
- Regarding Schrems II mitigations: we will provide the technical and organizational measures mapping (routing, access controls, logging minimization). For extra assurance, we offer a short architecture review where we can demonstrate per-tenant routing and KV cache boundaries.

2) KMS / CMEK
- Current state: CMSK/CMEK is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted customers we do not yet offer full customer-managed key exclusivity, but we can commit to a roadmap with milestones.
- Proposed procurement language: we can include a clause that Customer may request Dedicated or Private deployment with CMEK, and for Hosted we will use reasonable commercial efforts to add Hosted-CMEK within an agreed timeline (we propose Q4 2027 for feature GA).

3) Deletion and retention (including backups)
- Live deletion API: immediate.
- Persistent snapshots/backups: by default retained in-region; we will add explicit contract language that RegulaHealth data snapshots will not be copied outside EU for your tenant and that deletion requests will cascade to retention stores within a 60-day window (exceptions for legal hold will be documented).

4) Evidence and artifacts
- We'll furnish: SCCs annex (signed), controls catalogue (PDF), in-region routing evidence (architecture sketch + sample logs with redaction), and a deletion runbook.

Action items:
- Stephanie: confirm the 45-minute call for 2027-07-02 10:00 CEST.
- Laura: prepare formal attestation language for support access and logs.
- Ben: loop in billing/procurement for SOW and PO acceptance process.

Happy to hop on the call and walk through the technical artifacts.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
VP Privacy & Legal, Redwood Inference
